## Project: Jupyter Kernel Client

### What the README says

This is a Python library called **`jupyter-kernel-client`** by [Datalayer](https://datalayer.io), published on PyPI under the BSD 3-Clause License. Its purpose is to let you **connect to live Jupyter Kernels over HTTP and WebSocket**.

Key features described:

1. **`JupyterKernelClient`** — the main class. You point it at a running Jupyter Server (URL + token) and call `.execute(code)` to run code on a kernel. It can be used as a context manager (`with`) or with explicit `.start()` / `.stop()` calls. You can also attach to an **existing** kernel by supplying its `kernel_id`.

2. **Jupyter Konsole** — an optional interactive REPL (`jupyter konsole ...`) that connects to a kernel and gives an `In [1]:` prompt, installed via the `[konsole]` extra.

3. **Install / Uninstall** — plain `pip install jupyter_kernel_client` / `pip uninstall`.

4. **Contributing** — dev install with `pip install -e ".[konsole,test,lint,typing]"`, tests run with `pytest`.

---

### Repository layout

```
/
├── jupyter_kernel_client/   # Main Python package
│   ├── __init__.py          # Public exports
│   ├── __version__.py       # Version string
│   ├── client.py            # JupyterKernelClient (HTTP+WS kernel client)
│   ├── wsclient.py          # Low-level WebSocket client
│   ├── manager.py           # Kernel manager (create/delete kernels via HTTP)
│   ├── models.py            # Data models / typed structures
│   ├── interfaces.py        # Abstract interfaces / protocols
│   ├── constants.py         # Shared constants
│   ├── shell.py             # Shell channel handling
│   ├── konsoleapp.py        # `jupyter konsole` CLI entry point
│   ├── snippets.py          # Code snippet helpers
│   ├── log.py               # Logging setup
│   ├── utils.py             # Utility functions
│   └── tests/               # Test suite (run with pytest)
│
├── docs/                    # Docusaurus-based documentation site
├── dev/
│   └── test.ipynb           # Development/scratch notebook
├── .github/                 # GitHub Actions workflows (CI build)
├── pyproject.toml           # Package metadata & dependencies
├── Makefile                 # Convenience targets (jupyter-server, jupyterlab, etc.)
├── CHANGELOG.md             # Version history
├── RELEASE.md               # Release instructions
├── LICENSE                  # BSD 3-Clause
└── README.md
```

**In summary:** the repo is a focused Python library. All source lives in the `jupyter_kernel_client/` package, the docs site is a separate Docusaurus app under `docs/`, a single development notebook is in `dev/`, and standard Python packaging files (`pyproject.toml`, `Makefile`) sit at the root.
